question: Why did the p95 latency go up on 09 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: The flash sale campaign caused a sudden increase in request volume and error rate.
why_chain: The flash sale campaign went live at the change point, causing a surge in requests.
The surge in requests led to increased latency as the system could not handle the load.
The increased latency resulted in the observed rise in P95 latency.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The change was due to a configuration update.
ruled_out.reason: No evidence supports a configuration change.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in latency was due to a data quality issue.
ruled_out.reason: No evidence supports a data quality issue.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in latency was due to a dependency issue with an external service.
ruled_out.reason: No evidence supports a dependency issue with an external service.

evidence.summary: P95 latency for region ap-south rose from 137 ms to 290 ms (+112%), with a change point at 2026-03-09T09:05:00Z.
The change is concentrated in region ap-south: 4 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.01).
At the same time, request volume for region ap-south rose (1230 per 5 min before, 5151 per 5 min after, +319%).
At the same time, error rate for region ap-south rose (0.41% before, 0.80% after, +96%).
Marketing: flash sale campaign goes live in ap-south at 09:05 UTC (ap-south; 233 min before the change; record R011)
Request volume 3x normal in ap-south (ap-south; 12 min after the change; record R012)
autoscaler: scaling out, 4 new instances requested (ap-south; 20 min after the change; record R013)

reasons: ✓ A change event (tickets) lines up in time (233 min before the change).
✓ 2 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✓ Request volume rose, as a traffic cause requires.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.

actions.action: Implement a dynamic scaling strategy to better handle sudden spikes in traffic.
Monitor request volume and error rates closely during marketing campaigns to detect and respond to sudden spikes.
Optimize the autoscaler to better handle the load during sudden traffic spikes.
